newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt extends deadline for BOT container terminal.
newsitem.headline: Egypt extends deadline for BOT container terminal.

text.p: Egypt on Wednesday extended until May 27 the deadline for bids to build and run a container terminal in the Red Sea province of Suez under a BOT (build, operate, transfer) system. The original deadline was April 13.
The decision to postpone the deadline was taken in line with investors' requests, an official at the state's General Authority for Red Sea Ports (GARSP) told Reuters.
The authority also reduced the refundable deposit, which must accompany the bid, to 100,000 pounds ($29,500).
GARSPhad said the terminal would be at Adabiya port at the southern end of the Suez Canal. It "enjoys a unique location in Adabiya port and looks at Asia and Africa," it said.

The terminal includes quays 600 metres (2,000 feet) long and 15 metres (49 feet) deep and a storage area of 400,000 square metres (4.3 million square feet), it added. The quays length may be extended to 1,000 metres (3,280 feet).
The preliminary cost is expected to be 200 million pounds ($59 million), GARSP has said.
Egypt, facing tough competition from other regional traffic routes and declining Suez Canal revenues, is trying to build new free zones in Sinai and around the canal.
